title: Area of a rectangle
prompt: Write a function named rectangle_area that takes two arguments, length and width, and returns their product, which is the area of the rectangle. Do not print anything, return the value.

title: Whole minutes
prompt: Write a function named whole_minutes that takes one argument, total_seconds, a whole number that is zero or larger, and returns the number of complete minutes in it. Sixty seconds make one minute, and any leftover seconds are ignored. For example 130 seconds is 2 complete minutes. Return the number, do not print it.

title: Average of three numbers
prompt: Write a function named average_of_three that takes three numbers, a, b and c, and returns their average, that is their sum divided by 3. Use ordinary division so the answer keeps its decimal part. Return the number, do not print it.

title: Price label
prompt: Write a function named label_price that takes two arguments, item (a string) and price (a number), and returns a single string made of the item name, then the text " costs $", then the price. For example label_price("apple", 3) returns "apple costs $3". Remember that a number has to be turned into a string before it can be joined to other text. Return the string, do not print it.

title: Even number check
prompt: Write a function named is_even that takes one whole number, number, and returns True when that number is even and False when it is odd. A number is even when the remainder of dividing it by 2 is zero. Return the True or False value, do not print it.
